# Results — Study 160 (Skyscraper-Curse) on real data

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). One recipe — test whether
S&P 500 total returns in the 1, 2, and 3 years after each world-record skyscraper
completion underperform the unconditional baseline — measured against a random-day
Monte-Carlo control on the Shiller monthly S&P 500 dataset. As-of **2026-06-15**.*

## Data stamp

| Source | Window | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|
| Shiller S&P 500 monthly | 1871-01-01 to 2026-05-01 | `4434e71175a6` |

Annual compound total returns computed from Shiller's SP500 price index and Dividend
column (monthly). n = 156 annual observations (1872–2026).

## Event table — world-record completions in the S&P era (1957+)

| Year | Building | City | Height (m) | 1-yr fwd S&P | 2-yr fwd S&P | 3-yr fwd S&P |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1972 | WTC North Tower | New York | 417 | **-16.9%** | — | — |
| 1974 | Sears Tower | Chicago | 442 | **+38.2%** | — | — |
| 1998 | Petronas Twin Towers | Kuala Lumpur | 452 | **+21.6%** | — | — |
| 2004 | Taipei 101 | Taipei | 508 | **+7.1%** | — | — |
| 2010 | Burj Khalifa | Dubai | 828 | **+2.1%** | — | — |
| 2023 | Merdeka 118 | Kuala Lumpur | 679 | **+28.3%** | — | — |

n = **6** world-record completions in the S&P 500 era. Note: all "forward" windows
start in January of the year *after* the completion year (no look-ahead).

## The honest test — event windows vs unconditional baseline

| Horizon | Event mean | Unconditional | Delta | Event n | HAC t | Low-power? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **1 year** | **+13.4%** | +10.9% | **+2.5pp** | 6 | +3.11 | YES (n=6) |
| **2 years** | **+22.2%** | +23.0% | **-0.8pp** | 6 | +2.66 | YES (n=6) |
| **3 years** | **+31.0%** | +35.6% | **-4.6pp** | 6 | +3.09 | YES (n=6) |

Key observations:
- At **1 year**, the event mean is *above* the unconditional (+13.4% vs +10.9%). The
  Skyscraper Curse predicts below-average returns — the data shows the opposite.
- At **3 years**, the event mean is below unconditional (+31.0% vs +35.6%), but the
  difference is small and statistically undetectable at n=6.
- HAC t-stats look large (+3.11 for 1yr), but with n=6 the t-distribution has 5 degrees
  of freedom; |t| >= 2.015 is required for p < 0.10. More importantly, with 6 data
  points the *t-stat itself* is an unreliable estimate — the point is the power analysis.

## Random-day control (1-year horizon)

2,000 random draws of 6 starting years from the 1871-2026 tape, compared to the
observed event mean of +13.4%:

| | Value |
|---|---|
| Observed event mean (1yr) | +13.4% |
| Random control mean | +10.9% |
| Random control std | 7.3% |
| 90th percentile of random | +20.0% |
| 95th percentile of random | +22.2% |
| **Empirical p-value** | **0.614** |

The p-value of 0.614 means 61% of random 6-year bundles produce *worse* returns than
the skyscraper events. The events are not a bad omen — they are indistinguishable from
a random draw of years.

## Real (inflation-adjusted) returns

| | 1-yr mean | HAC t |
|---|---|---|
| Events (real) | +9.2% | +1.98 |
| Unconditional (real) | +8.6% | — |

Even on real returns, events outperform slightly — the curse is not there.

## Power analysis

At n=6 and the observed effect size (delta ~2-5 pp), statistical power is approximately
at the 5% noise floor. To reach 80% power at the observed unconditional spread would
require approximately n ~ 30-100 events. There will never be 30 world-record skyscrapers
in the S&P era. The Skyscraper Index is structurally untestable.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** Events outperform unconditional at 1-year (+2.5pp). No
  underperformance at any horizon. Random-day p = 0.614 (no signal). HAC t-stat is
  unreliable at n=6 (5 degrees of freedom, power ~5%).
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** 6 events over 50 years = 1 per decade. No actionable
  entry/exit rule. No meaningful backtest possible.
- **n too small — BUSTED.** Statistical power is ~5% (noise floor) at n=6. The
  hypothesis is structurally unverifiable with the available event count. This is a
  narrative dressed as a signal.
